problem: Prior VLN agents learn step-by-step from individual instruction-trajectory pairs, ignoring cross-instance similarities/differences and the temporal continuity of sub-instructions, so representations are not distinctive and generalize poorly to unseen environments.
motivation: Correct vs. wrong actions and similar vs. different instruction-trajectory pairs carry extra knowledge unused by standard imitation/RL training. Contrastive learning has improved generalization in vision, but had not been applied to VLN, and naive use suffers from easy-sample domination and false negatives.
key_idea: Add coarse-grained (whole trajectory and whole instruction) and fine-grained (sub-instruction) contrastive losses with augmented positives and intra/inter negatives, trained with a pair-mining plus circle-loss reweighting mechanism, on top of existing VLN agents.
insight: Each contrastive term improves the baseline on its own, and combining them is best (SPL 52.90 to 55.83 on R2R val-unseen, no speaker augmentation). Hard-sample mining and self-paced circle-loss weighting matter: circle loss + memory bank + pair mining reaches 55.47 SPL vs. 52.62 for multi-pair InfoNCE (which is sensitive to the number of augmented trajectories) and 53.14 without pair mining. Gains are larger with little training data (semi-supervised setting).
method: Trajectory coarse loss L_CT: sub-optimal trajectories with same start/end are positives if hops ≤ 1.2×optimal and intra-negatives if hops ≥ 1.4×optimal; inter-negatives come from a memory bank

Instruction coarse loss L_CI: positives from WordNet synonym substitution, BERT insert/substitute, and back-translation; intra-negatives from shuffled or repeated sub-instructions; memory bank of inter-negatives

Sub-instruction fine loss L_FI: a random sub-instruction is the query, its neighbouring sub-instructions are positives, non-neighbours are intra-negatives, and sub-instructions from other instructions are inter-negatives via memory bank
Pair mining: discard easy samples and false negatives (sim > 1-m) by comparing against the hardest positive/negative with margin m=0.25
Sample reweighting: circle loss with self-paced weights that give larger weight to pairs far from their optimum
Training: L = IL + RL(A2C) + 0.1·L_CT' + 0.01·L_CI' + 0.01·L_FI'; memory bank size 240; plugs into EnvDrop or RecBERT

setting.backbone: RecBERT (init OSCAR or PREVALENT) and EnvDrop, trained with CITL auxiliary losses
setting.training_data: R2R/R4R/RxR training sets plus the PREVALENT augmentation data for RecBERT; augmented trajectories/instructions generated for contrastive learning
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with candidate viewpoint views

numbers.extra: single run, greedy, no pre-exploration; PREVALENT augmentation data

results: CITL on RecBERT (init PREVALENT) reaches 63 SR / 58 SPL on R2R val-unseen and 64 SR / 59 SPL on test-unseen, about +2 SPL over RecBERT (57 on test). On R4R val-unseen SPL rises 31.7 to 35.1, and on RxR SR rises 44.9 to 47.2 and SPL 39.3 to 40.7.
limitations: Gains on strong baselines are modest (about 1 point SR/SPL on R2R val-unseen), and EnvDrop shows no val-unseen gain
Many hyperparameters (margins, alpha_p/alpha_n, memory size, lambdas) and augmentation pipelines are needed; only discrete-graph VLN is evaluated
R4R and RxR baselines are the authors' reproductions
